compliance.environment: Indoor use only, in environmentally controlled areas

physical.finish: Black epoxy-polyester hybrid powder coat paint on steel parts; black plastic
physical.material: Steel mid panels and splice plates, plastic sides, steel door with plastic hinges

base.description: The manager as Chatsworth ships 13915-701, all four doors fitted.

datasheet.title: Velocity Cable Management product data sheet (Rev.23 06/22)

description: Velocity double-sided vertical cable manager, Chatsworth Products 13915-701: a black plastic and steel manager 70 in (1778 mm) tall, 12 in (305 mm) wide and 17.8 in (446 mm) deep, for 6'H (1.8 m), 38U racks, that bolts to the side of the rack and stands beside it. Two channels 272 mm wide stand back to back, 191 mm deep at the front and 140 mm at the rear. Each has a wall of T-shaped fingers down each edge, one rack unit apart, and a steel door in two halves. It takes no rack unit.

gaps.note: the data sheet lists four steel mid panels with attachment points for cable management accessories and gives the usable depth of each channel; no held page draws or dimensions the panel, so the 75 mm between the two floors (406 less 191 less 140) is drawn as one solid plate with no attachment point or opening.
gaps.wanted: a dimensioned section of the manager

gaps.note: no held page draws the rear of a double-sided manager: the data sheet lists four half-height covers and a usable depth of 140 mm at the rear, and its one photograph shows the front. The rear channel is drawn as the front one at that depth, its fingers level with the front ones.
gaps.wanted: a dimensioned rear view or a section

gaps.note: no held page dimensions a finger: the arm and the head are read by eye from the page 2 drawing of the single-sided part, and the count (38 a side of each channel) is the rack's units.
gaps.wanted: a dimensioned side view of one section

gaps.note: the guide says the manager is two sections, equal for 6 ft and 8 ft and a short upper over a long lower for 7 ft; no held page gives the lengths, so the seam is drawn at the middle.
the doors swing open to the right or left and release when pulled from a corner; the format has no hinge, so each is drawn as one fitted plate and the swing is not stated.
gaps.wanted: a format that can say a hinged cover

gaps.note: the table's depth is the 406 without doors plus the bevel of the doors, which varies slightly with width; the two doors are taken as equal, each drawn as a flat plate standing 20 mm past the ends of the guides.
the manager bolts to the rack's upright with M8 bolts; how far it stands from the upright and whether it overlaps the rail is never dimensioned.
gaps.wanted: a dimensioned drawing of the manager fitted to a rack

gaps.note: the table's notes give the usable width (33 mm less than overall) and the usable depths (191 mm front, 140 mm rear); they do not say that the two finger walls are equal and are all of the 33, or that each depth runs from the floor to the ends of the guides, so the 16.5 mm wall and the 75 mm mid panel are derived with those assumptions.
gaps.wanted: a dimensioned section of the manager

gaps.note: the installation instructions held are for the single-sided 6 in part and none is held for a double-sided one; the section, finger and wall are those drawn there and are taken to hold at 12 in and on both faces. The data sheet photograph of the 12 in double-sided part (page 3) shows T-shaped guides down the front and supports the front only.
gaps.wanted: the installation instructions or a section of a double-sided part

gaps.note: the table prints 17.8 in and 446 mm for the depth, and 17.8 in is 452 mm. The millimetre figure is drawn as printed.
gaps.wanted: the maker's own figure for the part with its doors fitted

gaps.note: the data sheet's cable fill row points to the maker's cable fill table on its site and states no figure; that table is not held.

body.description: the back plates and the finger walls, the front channel first, left wall first

door.description: the four half-height doors, the front upper first, then the rear

fingers.description: the T-shaped fingers, 38 a side of each channel; the front channel's left wall top to bottom and then its right, then the rear channel

attrs.note: datasheet - material, finish, colour and the indoor-only statement are the specifications table (page 2) and the table's note 'Color is Black'.

bottom.note: estimated - the bottom end is the top end again.

chassis.note: datasheet - 70 in (1778 mm) high, 12 in (305 mm) wide and 17.8 in (446 mm) deep for 13915-701 in the ordering table. THE DEPTH IS THE TABLE'S, WITH THE BEVEL OF THE DOORS: the table's note says the manager is 16 in (406 mm) deep without doors, that the overall depth varies a little with width because of the bevel of the door, and that the usable depth is 7.5 in (191 mm) at the front and 5.5 in (140 mm) at the rear. So the guides end 406 apart and the two doors stand 20 beyond them if they are equal. THE TABLE'S TWO DEPTH FIGURES DISAGREE: it prints 17.8 in and 446 mm, and 17.8 in is 452 mm. The millimetre figure is drawn as printed; 452 would put the doors 23 mm out, which is what the 12 in single-sided part's bevel is, and move each door's rails by 3 mm.

color.note: estimated - 'Color is Black' (ordering table); the shade is the near-black of the maker's photographs of the fitted part, which are renders.

door.note: datasheet - four half-height covers that snap onto the T-shaped cable guides, two on each face, steel with plastic hinges on the 12 in manager (pages 1 and 2). They are drawn as one plate each, the seam at the middle of the height; for the 7 ft manager the installation instructions say the upper section is short and the lower long, and no page gives the lengths, so the seam is estimated there.

fingers.note: estimated - A FINGER TO EACH RACK UNIT, 38 A SIDE OF EACH CHANNEL. The data sheet says the T-shaped guides are 'spaced 1U apart' and the installation instructions show a column down each edge; no page counts them. 38 is the rack's units (6'H (1.8 m), 38U), a column centred on the height with 44.45 left at each end. A finger is an arm 14 high with a head 32 high, read by eye from the page 2 drawing of the single-sided part, and taken to be the same on every width and at the rear.

front.note: estimated - the front doors, fitted. With them off the front is the channel between the two finger walls, the ends of the fingers along each edge and the back plate at the bottom of it. The channel is 272 wide, the 305 overall less the 33 (1.3 in) the table's note takes off for the usable width, so each wall is 16.5 if the two walls are equal and are all of the 33, which no held page says.

guides.note: estimated - the duct on each face is the channel between its two finger walls, 272 wide, run down the height (`run: y`). Its finger pitch is the rack unit, 44.45; the gap between arms is the pitch less the arm's estimated 14.

left.note: estimated - the side, rear at x=0: each channel's wall root, 38 arms and heads at one rack unit and the edge of its two doors with the seam between them, and the mid panel between the two.

method.note: FIGURES FROM THE DATA SHEET TABLE; THE CONSTRUCTION FROM THE INSTALLATION DRAWINGS OF THE SINGLE-SIDED 6 IN PART. The Velocity Cable Management product data sheet (Rev.23 06/22) (page 3) prints the part as 70 x 12 x 17.8 in (1778 x 305 x 446 mm), shipping weight 40 lb (18.1 kg) as printed, for 6'H (1.8 m), 38U racks, with notes on depth and usable size, and page 1 lists what the double-sided kit holds. The Velocity Vertical Cable Manager installation instructions (IIS-713902, Rev. 2) draw how a single-sided Velocity manager is assembled, mounted and fitted with its doors; none is held for a double-sided part, and its construction is taken to hold here, on both faces, which the data sheet photograph of the 12 in double-sided part (page 3) supports for the T-shaped guides down the front and no page states for the rear. NO HELD PAGE DIMENSIONS THE PART INTERNALLY: a finger, the root of a wall, the door section and the mid panel are estimated, each in its own entry below. Nothing was copied from a picture; the figures are transcribed.

mount.note: drawing - rack-side. The installation instructions of the single-sided part (pages 1 and 4) have the manager positioned next to the rack and bolted to the rack's upright with M8 bolts through the manager's holes and the rack's front holes ('the top front rack hole'), eight M8 x 25 mm bolts in the kit, so it stands beside the rack, outside the rails, its fingers facing forward and back. It occupies no rack unit; `ru: 38` is the rack it is sold for ('For 6'H (1.8 m), 38U Racks').

rear.note: estimated - the rear channel, the same parts placed the same way as the front, at the rear usable depth of 140 (5.5 in): the data sheet lists four half-height covers and that usable depth, and the one photograph shows the front. Its fingers stand level with the front ones, which no page says. The rear is a working face, so no opening is drawn in it.

right.note: estimated - the left view mirrored: the manager is the same on both sides.

shell.note: drawing - TWO HOLLOW CHANNELS BACK TO BACK, NOT A BOX, as the dual-sided finger ducts already in the library are built. The body is a sheet body and its views are elevations; the solid is what its parts build: on each face the back plate as a well (211 deep at the front, 160 at the rear), the two finger walls, 38 fingers a wall standing in it and two half-height doors that pull off and open that channel. The two floors stand 75 apart in the middle of the part (see `spine`); plates sunk 0.05 inside the top, bottom and side faces close the mid panel between them.

spine.note: estimated - the mid panel is the 75 between the two floors: the table's note gives 406 deep without doors, 191 usable at the front and 140 at the rear, and 406 less the two is 75. This takes each usable depth to run from its floor to the ends of its guides, which the note does not say. The data sheet (page 1) lists four steel mid panels with attachment points; none is dimensioned, so the panel is drawn as one solid plate with no attachment point or opening.

thickness.note: estimated - no held page states a wall gauge. 1.5 is the plate of comparable parts in the library; the parts carry their own thicknesses.

top.note: estimated - the end of the manager seen from above, rear at y=0: the rear door to 3, its rails to 20, the rear heads to 29, the arms to 150, the wall roots to 160, the mid panel to 235, then the front wall roots, arms, heads, rails and door out to 446. The depths are the table's and the note's; the split is the estimate of the finger, the wall and the door.

weight.note: datasheet - 40 lb (18.1 kg) in the ordering table, whose column is SHIPPING weight: the carton is in it, so the manager itself weighs less. It is stated as the weight so the part has one, and is an upper bound.

references.title: Velocity Vertical Cable Manager installation instructions (IIS-713902, Rev. 2)

guides.source: Velocity data sheet page 3 note (usable width) and page 1 (fingers spaced 1U apart); the gap is the pitch less an estimated arm
